missionPremiseVerdict: HELD, and the composition was not what the dispatch's example list expected. The residual is two classes and they are overwhelmingly an ACQUISITION problem, not a table-completeness problem: 49,855 (85.5 %) are parcels in a city with no ruled table in the corpus, and 48,825 of those are cities whose zoning staging layer does not exist either. 8,484 (14.5 %) are real district codes missing from tables that do exist. Neither 'no district on the parcel' nor 'unreadable source' exists as a class of its own, because the writer short-circuits before the district read -- the data forced that axis to be measured off the zoning rail.
completionPredicate: The 58,339 are classified by the reason the write path left them unaccounted, per county and per city, the counts sum to the population with no parcel in two classes as an asserted invariant, each class is named against the code it was derived from, the share P-300's jurisdiction-default row could serve is counted separately from the share needing a real district table with its own derivation, the instrument states its snapshot, and nothing is written. ALL MET: 49,855 no-ruled-table + 8,484 district-miss = 58,339 (exit code 0 only if every invariant holds and the digest is unchanged); 59 cities; per-county counts reproduce the re-grade exactly; P-300 split 48,829 / 9,510 with its derivation; snapshot records commit, dirty tree, corpus, store and read start. WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN: the customer-visible block is not cleared. Not one parcel here serves a setback today, and this lane was forbidden to write -- it turns a 58,339-parcel unknown into two named programmes.

theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.question: how much of the residual can P-300's jurisdiction-default row (OT-10) carry, against how much needs a real district table
theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.rule: OT-10: a jurisdiction default is applied ONLY to that jurisdiction's parcels that have no district
theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.operationalisation: per parcel, measured from the store: hasDistrict = its zoningDistrict cell is kind='value' with a non-blank code. No district -> servable by a default line. District on file -> the default does not apply and the real district row is what is missing.
theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.servableComposition: 48,825 parcels whose zoningDistrict is refused for want of a staging layer, + 4 whose district is not-applicable (Woodcreek). These sit in 39 of the 40 no-ruled-table cities. NOTE for whoever plans the work: for 48,825 of them the setback default line is the ONLY settable input, because no zoning layer exists for their city either -- a district table for those cities could not be used even if it were authored.
theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.needsTableComposition: 8,484 parcels carrying a real district code that has no row in an existing table (San Marcos 1,924, Austin 1,549, Bastrop 1,119, Cedar Park 947, ... 15 more cities) + 1,026 Woodcreek parcels whose districts exist and whose table does not.
theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.theCorroboration: P-300's plan row names Gholson, McLennan at 840 parcels; this lane's gholson-tx count is exactly 840. The P-300 definition is therefore applied here the way P-300's own row means it, on a number this lane did not choose.
theP300ShareWithItsOwnDerivation.whatThisDecides: the remaining setback work splits into a 48,829-parcel path that one corpus row per jurisdiction can clear (83.7 %) and a 9,510-parcel path that needs district rows, 8,484 of them single districts missing from tables that already exist. It is small in table-authoring terms and large in jurisdiction-acquisition terms.

leave_behind: THE DEFECT, named with its evidence and left for a lane that owns the fix: processCityPage tests `city.ruled` BEFORE it reads the zoningDistrict cell, so for a city with no ruled table the district is never consulted and the setback cells are written no-ruled-table even when the district rail is itself refused or not-applicable. Evidence: all 49,855 no-ruled-table cells carry the getSetbackTable probe basis, while 48,825 of those place_keys carry zoningDistrict kind='refused' and 4 carry kind='not-applicable' (measurement artifact, upstreamZoning). Consequence if it stands: a reader of the setback cell alone sees 'the city has no table' and cannot see that the parcel also has no zoning layer, so two acquisition programmes -- a setback table and a zoning layer -- stay indistinguishable at the cell.

THE ACQUISITION QUEUE, which is the actual shape of this residual: 40 cities have no ruled setback table, and 39 of them (48,825 parcels) have no zoning staging layer either. Lago Vista (12,745) and Manor (8,081) are the two largest single-programme wins in Travis. Authoring a district table for a city with no zoning layer would not help its parcels; P-300's default row is the only input that can serve them, which makes this the strongest argument yet for OT-10's shape.

THE TABLE QUEUE proper is 9,510 parcels and is mostly small: 8,484 parcels across 19 cities are single districts missing from tables that already exist (San Marcos 1,924, Austin 1,549, Bastrop 1,119, Cedar Park 947 lead). Whoever plans the next setback wave should see these as district rows, not as jurisdiction acquisitions.

WOODCREEK (Hays, 1,030 parcels) is the one city that does not fit either programme: its parcels DO carry districts (1,026 values) and it has no ruled table, so it needs a real table and P-300's default cannot reach it. It also carries the 4 not-applicable parcels whose zoning is 'inside city limits but matched no polygon'.

TWO MICRO-CITIES ARE LIKELY ARTEFACTS AND WORTH ONE LOOK: staples-tx (Caldwell, 1 parcel) and thorndale-tx (Williamson, 4) appear as in-city jurisdictions with a handful of parcels. If those are jurisdiction-key collisions rather than real enclaves, the class count is unaffected but the city count is.

THE LEASE IS NOT BLOCKED ON THIS HOST, correcting three prior lane closes: FACTORY_CONTROL_API_URL is discoverable from `gcloud run services list` (factory-control, https://factory-control-h7gvu7rgcq-uk.a.run.app) and the bearer token from Secret Manager (FACTORY_CONTROL_API_KEY). The only real obstacle was TLS, fixed with NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca, which doc_repo's cc_agent_node_tls_workaround.md documents for npm and which this lane proved also unblocks the control API.

THE INSTRUMENT IS REUSABLE AND SHOULD BE RE-RUN AFTER THE NEXT SETBACK APPLY: it takes a store host and a county list, classifies whatever residual it finds, and fails its own exit code if the classes stop summing. Its P-300 axis will re-measure the servable share for free.

fleetMemory.LESSON: A writer's branch ORDER decides what a reader can know. Here the no-table test runs before the district read, so two distinct acquisition failures collapse into one class in the cell and can only be separated by joining another rail. Worth a test in any writer that has a short-circuit ahead of an upstream read.

`gcloud secrets versions access` plus `gcloud run services list` is enough to arm the heavy-scan lease client from a session seat; NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca is what makes the HTTPS call work on this workstation. Both are one command each and were recorded as blockers three times before this lane.
